transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (NovoPay Eng Mgr), Lena Ortiz (NovoPay SRE), Diego Morales (NovoPay ML)

Summary:
Quick POV review of last week's throughput runs, discuss tuning changes (concurrency targets, continuous batching, queueing), agree on next soak and ownership. Some minor transcription errors in places; speaker overlaps.

Topics:
- Throughput runs recap (p50/p95 latency, qps achieved)
- Continuous batching behavior under bursty traffic
- Concurrency targets per model/route
- Queueing/backpressure and fallback configs
- Next soak and deliverables

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, uh we'll keep this tight 30 to 45, um so quick agenda, recap the runs you shared, then tuning recs, then next steps.
[00:18] Samir Patel: cool thanks Alex, a quick note, we ran the 300 qps test overnight on the dedi pool, um results were kinda, mixed, p95 spiked to 1.2s when latency sensitive route had bursts, but average token cost was lower, so trade-off.
[00:34] Priya Nair: right, that's what we saw in our bench - continuous batching helped throughput but on short-latency tail it could add headroom so we need tight concurrency caps and low queuing for the low-latency route.
[00:50] Lena Ortiz: clarification, when you say concurrency caps do you mean per-model or per-route, we have two main routes: auth-check (very latency sensitive) and summary-gen (more throughput tolerant).
[01:05] Priya Nair: per-route ideally; per-model is coarser. so auth-check gets concurrency 4 and small batch timeout, summary-gen gets concurrency 24 and higher batch window, something like that.
[01:20] Diego Morales: can you explain the batch timeout, like 5ms vs 20ms change the behavior, I'm fuzzy on exact numbers.
[01:28] Alex Chen: sure, so the engine collects tokens up to max batch size or until batch timeout fires. with continuous batching, if there's steady stream, batches form quickly; with bursts, timeout helps gather more. small timeout reduces tail but hurts throughput. it's a balance.
[01:48] Samir Patel: our logs show long queues at 2am but throughput stayed stable; p95 jumped when a big spike hit auth-check, I think there was queueing spilling into that route.
[02:01] Priya Nair: sounds like routing/muxing rule needed - you can reserve a small pool or set route priority so auth-check doesn't get queued behind heavy summary-gen traffic. Redwood supports route-level pool pinning and automatic fallback.
[02:18] Lena Ortiz: how invasive is pool pinning for our infra? we wanted minimal infra changes.
[02:24] Priya Nair: it's config only, you can pin route to dedicated subset of capacity, or set a soft reservation which prioritizes requests but allows bursts to borrow capacity if free.
[02:36] Diego Morales: what about KV cache? we turned it on for summary-gen but not auth-check. any numbers on hit rates?
[02:42] Alex Chen: preliminary stats from last run: summary-gen KV hit ~42% which reduced token generation by ~35% and improved effective qps, auth-check not cached. we'll get a detailed table but those are rough.
[02:58] Samir Patel: ok good. i want to see cache vs no-cache runs because we saw weird latencies with cache cold starts.
[03:06] Priya Nair: noted, we'll run controlled benchmark to compare warm cache, cold cache, and no cache.
[03:12] Alex Chen: on concurrency recs - for your model (redwood-7b-ish) with 512 context, baseline concurrency per GPU was hitting memory sweet spot at 16 concurrent streams; with q4 quant we saw 20 streams before OOM risk. but per-route we recommend 4 for auth-check, 18-20 for summary-gen if you want max throughput.
[03:36] Diego Morales: can you repeat q4 quant impact? we use q4-hf.
[03:40] Priya Nair: q4 reduces memory footprint so you can raise concurrency; but perf per token slightly different, also kernel choice matters. small models might not benefit as much.
[03:52] Samir Patel: another ask - how does the autoscaler interact with pinned pools? we had scale delays overnight.
[03:59] Alex Chen: autoscaler looks at queue depth and token throughput, with pinned pools there's a separate scaling policy. autoscaler cooldown default is 2m, we can reduce for your sandbox to 30s for the soak.
[04:12] Lena Ortiz: i worry about flapping if cooldown low.
[04:15] Priya Nair: we can set conservative min replicas to avoid oscillation, so reduce cooldown but set floor replicas to keep warm capacity.
[04:24] Diego Morales: about queueing strategies - is there support for backpressure and early reject? sometimes better to 429 than spike p95.
[04:34] Alex Chen: yes you can set hard queue limit, and Redwood can respond with 429 or route to fallback lighter model. we can demo fallback in next run.
[04:44] Samir Patel: fallback to smaller model might change quality, we need to track metrics.
[04:48] Priya Nair: absolutely, Redwood Optimize can tie quality regression alerts to prompt sets, so fallback events trigger evals and a slack webhook we configured.
[04:58] Alex Chen: for this week's plan - we recommend three experiments: 1) Run KV cache vs no-cache for summary-gen with 500 qps for 1 hour, 2) Run 2-hour soak at 500 qps with pinned small pool for auth-check route to validate concurrency 4, 3) Run 4-hour soak on dedicated pool with concurrency 18-20 for summary-gen to measure cost/unit.
[05:22] Samir Patel: timeline? we can provision sandbox today.
[05:24] Priya Nair: if you provision now, we can start bench tomorrow, Alex will share config and scripts.
[05:30] Diego Morales: can you also share the benchmark harness you used, we have our own but want parity.
[05:34] Alex Chen: yes, i'll share a link to the harness and a small script to replay traffic with same distribution.
[05:40] Lena Ortiz: small nit - some of our logs had Redwood product name misspelled as redwood-infernce in our notes, not a blocker.
[05:46] Alex Chen: (laughs) we've seen worse.
[05:50] Priya Nair: a couple of micro recs on tuning: set batch timeout to 8ms for auth-check and 30ms for summary-gen, set max batch size 32 for auth-check and 128 for summary-gen, and enable continuous batching for both but with route-level constraints. also enable prefix KV caching for summary-gen.
[06:15] Diego Morales: that matches our intuition. also question - concurrency targets per GPU or per replica?
[06:22] Priya Nair: per replica concurrency leads to per-GPU when you place one replica per GPU; your infra mostly uses one replica mapped to a GPU, so it's equivalent. but if you colocate replicas on multi-gpu nodes it's different.
[06:36] Samir Patel: can you put the exact config as a yaml? we prefer that for our infra team.
[06:41] Alex Chen: yes will send YAML with comments.
[06:44] Priya Nair: action items: we'll run KV benchmark and concurrency runs, Alex will share configs and the harness, customer to provision sandbox.
[06:53] Samir Patel: onboarding internal stakeholders - i'll loop in infra lead after we see results.
[06:57] Alex Chen: cool. any blockers or risks?
[07:00] Lena Ortiz: main risk is noisy neighbor on shared cloud stage, but sandbox should isolate. also SOC2 checklist in process but not blocking bench.
[07:09] Diego Morales: also want to validate billing impact - can you provide expected cost delta estimates for changing concurrency/batches?
[07:16] Priya Nair: yes we'll provide rough cost-per-1k-requests estimates based on token reduction from KV hits and concurrency adjustments.
[07:25] Alex Chen: ok recap: Priya runs KV vs no-cache and concurrency benchmarks (due 3/26); Alex sends YAML + harness + tuned recs (due 3/26); Samir provisions sandbox and shares creds (due 3/25); schedule soak for 3/29 tentative.
[07:45] Samir Patel: sounds good thanks all.
[07:48] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in slack and drop artifacts in the shared drive. bye.

End of transcript.
